primary_work.title: Modeling Unseen Environments with Language-guided Composable Causal Components in Reinforcement Learning
primary_work.official_code_status: no official repository linked on inspected paper/project pages as of 2026-07-25

finding: WM3C already covers block-wise identifiability of language-controlled latent dynamics when language components, disjoint target blocks, smooth invertible mixing, conditional independence, and sufficient component-wise variation are assumed. It does not jointly identify raw-language equivalence/factorization and unknown latent intervention partitions.
counterexample: Without a fixed population grammar and restrictions on language-to-dynamics mechanisms, any hidden component tuple can be bijectively re-encoded as one utterance factor, or one utterance ID can be invertibly split into pseudo-components, producing the same raw-string/trajectory distribution with different block counts and partitions.
remaining_rq: Under a specified population grammar and restricted non-lookup language-to-dynamics mechanism, jointly identify an unseen-form language factorization and a refinement of an intervention-induced causal abstraction when neither language components nor target blocks are supplied.
rejection_conditions: permits utterance-ID lookup or bijective recoding
does not prevent arbitrary component split/merge
is a special case of WM3C or auxiliary-variable/multi-view CRL
lacks unseen-form and unseen-composition population split
lacks positive theorem and matched impossibility result
